# “What Do You Mean by That?” A Parser-Independent Interactive Approach for Enhancing Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#piia)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.561.pdf) · EMNLP 2020 proceedings, pages 6913-6922

**Reading coverage:** All ten PDF pages: Sections 1-8, equations, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-6 and captions, modifier examples and references. No appended supplement in this version.

## Research question

Improve a black-box Text-to-SQL parser by resolving expressions it fails to align with the generated SQL.

## Method

Restates SQL through templates, aligns question and restatement tokens with a weakly trained BERT model, asks ranked multiple-choice questions, and rewrites the original question with POS-dependent rules. Database contents are not read.

## Evaluation

Five parsers on WikiSQL and Spider. Simulation filters options using reference SQL and searches up to 100 combinations. A separate 300-question Spider study involves 30 non-SQL-expert volunteers, three judgments per question.

## What the results support

Human interaction raises IRNet and IRNet+BERT exact-match accuracy by 3.7 and 1.5 percentage points, respectively. Simulation reports larger gains. Rule-based rewriting outperforms direct token replacement in the tested IRNet setup.

## Limits and qualifications

The reference-assisted simulator is an idealized selection procedure. Candidate menus, supported SQL restatement grammar and modifier rules restrict generality; None preserves unchanged text but cannot ensure the intended option is offered.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides a black-box clarification interface and measured human/simulator gap, not a general answerability detector.
